<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="אלול_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518920167_theRebbe_725" batchId="meluket-_D7_90_D7_9C_D7_95_D7_9C_meluket__BH_POST_1766518920167_theRebbe_725__p003">
  <section v="6">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The maamar explains the difference between "receiving with a pleasant countenance" and "showing a smiling face," and how the latter reveals a higher, essential delight that transcends the arousal of repentance.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">5)</t>
    <t s="1">And it adds in the maamar, "and shows a smiling face to everyone,"</t>
    <t s="2">for the difference between "receives"</t>
    <t s="3">(with a pleasant countenance)</t>
    <t s="4">and "shows"</t>
    <t s="5">(a smiling face)</t>
    <t s="6">is,</t>
    <t s="7">that the term "receives" applies to something that exists beforehand</t>
    <t s="8">(before he received it)</t>
    <t s="9">and he receives that thing,</t>
    <t s="10">while "showing a smiling face" is that his smiling face</t>
    <t s="11">(which exists even before he shows it)</t>
    <t s="12">he shows and reveals to his fellow.</t>
    <t s="13">And this is that after it says that the king receives everyone with a pleasant countenance, it adds that he shows a smiling face to everyone,</t>
    <t s="14">for this that he receives them with a pleasant countenance is that the will of the people</t>
    <t s="15">(to greet the king)</t>
    <t s="16">is received by the king with a pleasant countenance,</t>
    <t s="17">and the addition of "shows a smiling face" is that when one is aroused in will to repent, there is drawn to him the revelation of the smiling face from above,</t>
    <t s="18">the delight</t>
    <t s="19">(laughter)</t>
    <t s="20">of the king himself.</t>
    <t s="21">For this delight is above the delight</t>
    <t s="22">(of the aspect of a pleasant countenance)</t>
    <t s="23">that comes from the arousal of repentance,</t>
    <t s="24">and as explained elsewhere,</t>
    <t s="25">that the root of laughter</t>
    <t s="26">(smiling face)</t>
    <t s="27">is in the essence of delight</t>
    <t s="28">(essential delight that is not composite)</t>
    <t s="29">which is above delight that comes through something</t>
    <t s="30">(composite delight).</t>
  </section>
  <section v="7">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The smiling face in the analogy refers to the delight in G-dliness inherent in Israel themselves, which when revealed, awakens in the person a corresponding essential delight in G-dliness, empowering complete repentance.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="1">that the matter of a smiling face in the analogue is the supernal delight that is in Israel themselves</t>
    <t s="2">(which is above the delight from the fulfillment of Torah and mitzvos of Israel,</t>
    <t s="3">and above also the delight from the service of repentance)</t>
    <t s="4">for this delight is in the Essence [Atzmus].</t>
    <t s="5">And by his showing them a smiling face,</t>
    <t s="6">that this delight is revealed to the person</t>
    <t s="7">(who is aroused with a will to repent),</t>
    <t s="8">this awakens in him</t>
    <t s="9">(as in water, face to face)</t>
    <t s="10">the delight in G-dliness, until the delight in G-dliness is the very essence of his delight,</t>
    <t s="11">and this gives him even more strength to overcome obstacles and hindrances and to return in complete repentance.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="8">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>From the above it is understood that the revelation in Elul is not only a grant of power for service, but also awakens the person, yet the service in Elul is still "I am to my Beloved," the work of man.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">6)</t>
    <t s="1">And it must be understood,</t>
    <t s="2">that from the above it is understood that the revelation in Elul is not only a granting of power for service</t>
    <t s="3">[for when the king is in the field there is permission and ability for everyone to greet him]</t>
    <t s="4">but also awakens the person</t>
    <t s="5">[for by the king receiving everyone with a pleasant countenance, and especially by his showing a smiling face to everyone,</t>
    <t s="6">this awakens them to return in complete repentance],</t>
    <t s="7">and nevertheless the service in Elul is "I am to my Beloved,"</t>
    <t s="8">the service of man.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
